title: Cinematography and Video Synthesis
answer: Text to video, virtual lensing, digital doubles, storyboarding and frame interpolation.

children.name: Text to Video, Physics and Continuity
children.blurb: Text to video with a focus on physics and continuity covers systems that turn a written prompt into a moving image sequence while keeping the result physically plausible and visually consistent from frame to frame.

sections.body: Cinematography and video synthesis covers making moving images with AI, from generating clips from text to controlling virtual cameras, replacing faces, planning shots, and repairing frames. Current work is practical and narrow: models produce short clips, often a few seconds, with visible artifacts in motion, lighting, and object permanence. Text to video systems turn a written prompt into a sequence of frames, but they do not yet hold a consistent world across long takes. Virtual lensing lets a director move a simulated camera through a scene after it is generated, and face replacement swaps one performer's likeness onto another's body for dubbing or de-aging. Storyboarding tools turn scripts into rough shot lists, and frame interpolation fills missing frames between existing ones for slow motion or restoration.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The honest limits are clear. No system here reliably maintains physical continuity, so objects change shape, hands drift, and backgrounds flicker between frames. Text to video is solved only for very short, stylized clips, not for narrative scenes with dialogue and blocking. Virtual camera work is promising but still constrained by the geometry the model guessed, which can warp when the view moves far from the original. Face replacement and digital doubles work well in controlled, well-lit footage but fail on fast motion, occlusions, or extreme angles. Frame interpolation is the most mature piece, used in broadcast and restoration, but it still invents detail that was never filmed, especially in fine textures like hair or fabric. This atlas currently tracks zero live video models and zero AI tools, so the pages describe methods and known failure modes rather than a catalog of shipping products.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader should start with Text to Video, Physics and Continuity, because it explains the core generation problem that every other page depends on. From there, Virtual Camera and Lensing shows how a generated or captured scene can be re-framed after the fact, which matters for directors who want control beyond the first output. Face Replacement and Digital Doubles covers the actor-focused side, where identity is swapped or preserved, and it connects to the continuity page through the need for stable facial tracking. Storyboarding and Pre-visualization is the earliest stage in a production, turning a script into rough moving images before any final render, and it relies on the same text to video techniques but with lower fidelity expectations. Frame Interpolation and Restoration sits at the end of the pipeline, repairing or extending footage that already exists, and it is the most practical entry point for archivists and editors.
